At today's September event, Apple officially unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo, but did not simultaneously announce the standard iPhone 18. The reasons will be explained later.

The standard iPhone 18 is expected to launch in early 2027, as Apple has adjusted the release schedule for its new products.

Generally speaking, today's Apple event should have been called the "iPhone 18 launch event."

However, Apple's arrangements surprised many — they did not announce the iPhone 18 today, at least not the standard version.

This time, Apple only launched three high-end new iPhones: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Duo.

This flagship lineup is clearly different from Apple's past practice: new standard iPhone models have always been announced alongside the Pro models. However, reports as early as May 2025 had foreshadowed this change.

According to multiple reports, the three new iPhones Apple launched today will be joined by three more new devices in early 2027:

  • iPhone 18
  • iPhone 18e
  • iPhone Air 2

Therefore, the standard iPhone 18 has not been cancelled — it is simply launching later than usual.

Why is there this change?

One explanation is that Apple hopes to expand the iPhone product line with new models such as the Duo foldable, and does not want to launch too many products all at once in the autumn. Splitting the main iPhone launches into autumn and spring cycles could be more advantageous.

Another possible reason is that Apple foresaw the current memory shortage long ago, knowing that if the standard iPhone 18 were launched alongside the Pro and Duo models, it would be difficult to meet market demand.

Regardless, the iPhone 18 will eventually arrive — just not until early 2027.

What are your thoughts on Apple's approach of splitting the iPhone 18 lineup into two phases? Feel free to share with us in the comments section.
